title: Video- The Norman Door with Vox

sentences.en: There's this door on the 10th floor of the Vox Media office that I hate so much.
sentences.zh: Vox Media 办公楼 10 楼有扇门，我讨厌死它了。

sentences.en: God damn it.
sentences.zh: 该死。

sentences.en: Do you ever get this door wrong?
sentences.zh: 你们也会经常推错这扇门吗？

sentences.en: Pretty regularly.
sentences.zh: 还挺经常的。

sentences.en: Have you seen people misuse it?
sentences.zh: 你见过别人用错它吗？

sentences.en: All the time, every day.
sentences.zh: 经常，每天都见。

sentences.en: Constantly.
sentences.zh: 一直都有。

sentences.en: I hate this door.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌这扇门。

sentences.en: Me too, Kelsey.
sentences.zh: 我也是，凯尔西。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题是这样的。

sentences.en: As soon as you start looking for confusing doors, they are everywhere.
sentences.zh: 只要你开始留意那些设计反人类的门，就会发现它们到处都是。

sentences.en: It's push.
sentences.zh: 这扇得推。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: I feel like Roman Mars would know about this.
sentences.zh: 我觉得罗曼·马尔斯可能会懂这个。

sentences.en: This is 99% invisible, and those doors you hate are called Norman door.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%无形》，而那些你讨厌的门被称为诺曼门。

sentences.en: Um, what's a Norman door?
sentences.zh: 呃，什么是诺曼门？

sentences.en: Don Norman wrote the essential book about design.
sentences.zh: 唐·诺曼写过一本关于设计的经典著作。

sentences.en: He is the Norman of the Norman door.
sentences.zh: 他就是诺曼门的那个“诺曼”。

sentences.en: All right, and where is this guy?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那这个人现在在哪？

sentences.en: You must go to San Diego.
sentences.zh: 你得去一趟圣迭戈。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I'm Don Norman.
sentences.zh: 我是唐·诺曼。
我是……

sentences.en: Gee, you know, it's hard to describe what I am.
sentences.zh: 天哪，你知道的，我很难形容我到底是干什么的。

sentences.en: Well, he's been a professor of psychology, professor of cognitive science,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他曾担任过心理学教授、认知科学教授、

sentences.en: professor of computer science, a vice president of advanced technology at Apple, but for our purposes.
sentences.zh: 计算机科学教授，还是苹果公司先进技术副总裁，不过就我们今天的主题而言。

sentences.en: I was spending a year in England, and I got so frustrated with my inability to use the light switches and the water taps,
sentences.zh: 我当时在英国呆了一年，对电灯开关、水龙头

sentences.en: and the doors, even, that I wrote this book.
sentences.zh: 甚至连门都用不好感到无比沮丧，于是我写了这本书。

sentences.en: If I continually get a door wrong, is it my fault?
sentences.zh: 如果我总是开错门，是我的错吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: In fact, if you continually get it wrong, it's a good...
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你一直开错，那说明……

sentences.en: And if other people continually get it wrong, it's a good sign that it's a really bad door.
sentences.zh: 如果其他人也一直开错，那就充分说明这是一扇真的很烂的门。

sentences.en: A Norman door is one where the design tells you to do the opposite of what you're actually supposed to do,
sentences.zh: 诺曼门是指那种设计引导你做出与实际操作完全相反行为的门，

sentences.en: or gives the wrong signal and needs a sign to correct it.
sentences.zh: 或者说它给出了错误的信号，需要贴个标志来纠正。

sentences.en: Why does it need an instruction manual?
sentences.zh: 为什么它还需要一本说明书？

sentences.en: That is, why do you have to have a sign that says push or pull?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，为什么非得搞个写着“推”或“拉”的牌子？

sentences.en: Why not make it obvious?
sentences.zh: 为什么不直接设计得一目了然呢？

sentences.en: It can be obvious, if it's designed right.
sentences.zh: 只要设计得当，它完全可以一目了然。

sentences.en: There are a couple of really simple, basic principles of design, and one of them I'll call discoverability.
sentences.zh: 设计有几个非常简单、基本的原则，其中一个我称之为“可发现性”。

sentences.en: When I look at something, I should be able to discover what operations I can do.
sentences.zh: 当我看着某样东西时，我应该能一眼看出我可以对它进行什么操作。

sentences.en: The principle applies to a whole lot more than doors.
sentences.zh: 这个原则不仅适用于门，还适用于很多其他事物。

sentences.en: And it's amazing with many of our computer systems today, you look at it, there's no way of knowing what's possible.
sentences.zh: 神奇的是，我们现在的很多计算机系统，你看一眼，根本无法知道有哪些功能。

sentences.en: Should I tap it once or twice, or even triple tap?
sentences.zh: 我应该点一下、点两下，还是点三下？

sentences.en: So discoverability, when it's not there, well, you don't know how to use something.
sentences.zh: 所以，一旦缺乏可发现性，你就不知道该怎么使用它了。

sentences.en: Another is feedback.
sentences.zh: 另一个原则是反馈。

sentences.en: And so many times there's no feedback.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候根本没有任何反馈。

sentences.en: You have no idea what happened, or why it happened.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道发生了什么，也不知道为什么会这样。

sentences.en: And these principles form the basis of how designers and engineers work today,
sentences.zh: 这些原则构成了当今设计师和工程师工作的基础，

sentences.en: commonly known as user- or human-centered design.
sentences.zh: 也就是通常所说的以用户或以人为本的设计。

sentences.en: I decided at one point the word user was a bit degrading.
sentences.zh: 我曾一度觉得“用户”这个词有点贬义。

sentences.en: Why not call people, people?
sentences.zh: 为什么不把人直接叫做人呢？

sentences.en: And it's amazingly simple and amazingly seldom practiced.
sentences.zh: 这个道理极其简单，却极少被付诸实践。

sentences.en: We call it iterative because it sort of goes around in a circle.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为迭代，因为它就像是一个不断循环的过程。

sentences.en: We go out and we observe what is happening today.
sentences.zh: 我们走出去，观察当下正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: We observe people doing the task.
sentences.zh: 我们观察人们执行任务的过程。

sentences.en: And from that, we say, oh, we have some ideas.
sentences.zh: 并由此产生一些想法。

sentences.en: Here's what we should perhaps propose to do.
sentences.zh: 比如我们接下来或许可以这样尝试。

sentences.en: Then you prototype your solution and test it.
sentences.zh: 然后你制作出解决方案的原型并进行测试。

sentences.en: Quite often these are wrong at firSt.
sentences.zh: 这些方案最初往往都是错的。

sentences.en: But each time we go around the circle, we do a better job of making the device
sentences.zh: 但每一次循环，我们都能把设备改进得更好一点，

sentences.en: until the point we're actually making something that really works.
sentences.zh: 直到最终做出真正好用的东西。

sentences.en: And this process has spread all over the world.
sentences.zh: 这个过程已经在全世界推广开来。

sentences.en: And it turns out it's improving lives.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，它正在改善人们的生活。

sentences.en: From better everyday things like the ones that Don wrote about.
sentences.zh: 从唐所写过的那种更好的日常物品开始。

sentences.en: To using the same process to solve huge problems in public health in developing countries.
sentences.zh: 到利用同样的流程来解决发展中国家公共卫生领域的巨大难题。

sentences.en: Water.
sentences.zh: 水资源。

sentences.en: Sanitation.
sentences.zh: 环境卫生。

sentences.en: Farming.
sentences.zh: 农业。

sentences.en: Lots more.
sentences.zh: 还有很多很多。

sentences.en: So what would be a better human-centered door?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么才是一扇真正以人为本的好门呢？

sentences.en: An ideal door is one that as I walk up to it and walk through it,
sentences.zh: 理想的门是这样的：当我走近并穿过它时，

sentences.en: I'm not even aware that I had opened the door and shut it.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都意识不到自己刚刚开门和关门。

sentences.en: So if you had a door which had a flat plate, what could you do?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有一扇装有平板的门，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都不用做。

sentences.en: The only thing you can do is push.
sentences.zh: 你唯一能做的就是推。

sentences.en: So see, you wouldn't need a sign.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，根本不需要什么标志。

sentences.en: A flat plate, you push.
sentences.zh: 平整的板，推就行了。

sentences.en: This kind of push bar with the piece sticking out on one side works well too.
sentences.zh: 这种一侧带有凸起杆的推杆也很好用。

sentences.en: So you can see what side you're supposed to push on.
sentences.zh: 这样你一眼就能看出该推哪一边。

sentences.en: Vertical bars could go either way.
sentences.zh: 垂直的把手则两边都可以。

sentences.en: A simple little hand thing though sort of indicates pull.
sentences.zh: 不过，一个小巧的手柄形状基本上暗示了这是用来拉的。

sentences.en: But we still have terrible, terrible doors in the world.
sentences.zh: 但这个世界上依然有无数糟糕透顶的门。

sentences.en: So many of them.
sentences.zh: 实在是太多了。

sentences.en: There are lots of things in life that are fairly standardized.
sentences.zh: 生活中的很多东西都已经高度标准化了。

sentences.en: And therefore, whether I buy this house or not is not a function or whether it has good doors in it.
sentences.zh: 因此，我买不买这栋房子，并不取决于它里面的门设计得好不好。

sentences.en: And so, except for safety reasons, doors tend not to be improved.
sentences.zh: 所以，除了出于安全原因，门往往不会有什么改进。

sentences.en: But the tyranny of bad doors must end.
sentences.zh: 但是，烂门带来的暴政必须终结。

sentences.en: I think that it's a really shitty design.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这设计简直烂透了。

sentences.en: In fact, they put a pull handle when it's a push.
sentences.zh: 明明该推的门，他们却装了个拉手。

sentences.en: And that should be a flat panel right here.
sentences.zh: 这里本来应该是一个平板才对。

sentences.en: And not a bull handle.
sentences.zh: 而不是一个拉手。

sentences.en: That's how I feel about the store.
sentences.zh: 这就是我对这家店的看法。

sentences.en: It's very misleading.
sentences.zh: 太具有误导性了。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: You're right, Becky.
sentences.zh: 贝基，你说的对。

sentences.en: You're goddamned right.
sentences.zh: 你他妈说得太对了。

sentences.en: And if we all thought like you, well, we might just design a better world together.
sentences.zh: 如果我们大家的想法都和你一样，那我们说不定真能一起设计出一个更美好的世界。

sentences.en: It won't open because it's a security door.
sentences.zh: 它打不开，因为这是一扇安全门。

sentences.en: What the f*** are you two doing?
sentences.zh: 你们两个他妈的在干什么？

sentences.en: Hey, this is Joe from Vox.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Vox 的乔。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for watching.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家的观看。

sentences.en: If you want to see more stuff like this, just come check us out at youtube.com slash Vox, V-O-X.
sentences.zh: 如果你想看更多这样的内容，欢迎访问 youtube.com/Vox，即 V-O-X。

sentences.en: It was so much fun collaborating with 99% Visible.
sentences.zh: 能和《99%无形》合作真的非常开心。

sentences.en: As you can see, there's some improvements being made over here, but obviously not as improved as it could be.
sentences.zh: 如你所见，这里已经做了一些改进，但显然还没改到最完美的地步。
